extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for handling preliminary, supplemental, and post-final amendments and replies to Office actions (when to enter or deny entry, required content, timing rules, and examiner actions). Focused on MPEP § 714 procedures and related CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization for examiner’s amendment when reply places case in condition for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply to a final Office action substantially places the application in condition for allowance, an examiner may request that the applicant authorize an examiner’s amendment to correct the omission and place the application in condition for allowance; the date of the reply is the date of such authorization (not the date the incomplete reply was filed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may also enter the reply, withdraw finality, and issue a new Office action (non-final, final, or action closing prosecution under Ex parte Quayle) at examiner's discretion. It is applicant’s responsibility to take necessary action to provide a complete reply under 37 CFR 1.113.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment definition and disapproval factors (37 CFR 1.115)
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment is received on or before the mail date of the first Office action (§ 1.104) and will be entered unless disapproved by the Commissioner. A preliminary amendment may be disapproved if it unduly interferes with preparation of a first Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors considered for disapproval include (i) the state of preparation of the first Office action as of the receipt date (§ 1.6) and (ii) the nature of changes to the specification or claims that would result from entry of the preliminary amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe-harbor timing for entry of preliminary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment will not be disapproved if filed no later than certain statutory time periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These include: (i) three months from the filing date of an application under 37 CFR 1.53(b); (ii) three months from the date the national stage is entered under 37 CFR 1.491; (iii) the filing date of a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d); and (iv) the last day of any suspension period requested under 37 CFR 1.103. These time periods are not extendable (37 CFR 1.115(c)). Entry should not be disapproved if within these periods even if examiner has spent significant time preparing the first Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of second (or subsequent) supplemental replies (37 CFR 1.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: A second (or subsequent) supplemental reply will be entered unless disapproved by the Commissioner, but may be disapproved if it unduly interferes with an Office action being prepared in response to the previous reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors to consider mirror those for preliminary amendments: state of preparation of the responsive Office action at receipt and the nature of any changes to specification or claims resulting from entry. Applicants are encouraged to include a complete reply in the first reply to prevent supplemental replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example of denying entry for supplemental reply
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner has nearly completed the Office action and a later supplemental reply (e.g., third reply) adds numerous claims requiring an updated prior art search, the examiner with SPE approval may deny entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This illustrates practical application of the 'unduly interferes' standard where significant additional examiner work would be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-prong test for denying entry of amendments/replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry of a preliminary amendment or second (or subsequent) supplemental reply may be denied if both conditions are met: (A) the examiner has devoted a significant amount of time to prepare an Office action before receipt, and (B) entry of the amendment or reply would require significant additional time to prepare the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once both conditions are met, the examiner should obtain SPE approval before denying entry. The list of illustrative items that may trigger the second prong is not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of content that may satisfy 'requires significant additional time'
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry may require significant additional time if the amendment or reply: (A) amends the claims; (B) adds numerous new claims; (C) amends the specification to change claim scope; (D) amends the specification raising new matter; (E) includes arguments; (F) includes an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 or 1.132; or (G) includes evidence traversing rejections from a prior Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list is illustrative; other situations satisfying the two-prong test may also justify denial of entry. SPE approval is required before denying entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: When disapproval of entry is inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Denying entry is inappropriate if either (A) the examiner has NOT devoted a significant amount of time prior to receipt, or (B) entry would NOT require significant additional time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if examiner has spent significant time, disapproval is not appropriate where the amendment merely cancels pending claims; amends claims to overcome 35 U.S.C. § 112, second paragraph; amends claims to place the application in condition for allowance; or only includes changes previously suggested by the examiner and would not require significant additional time to revise the Office action. In general, the amendment or reply will be entered unless denied for other listed reasons (e.g., MPEP § 714.19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies not fully responsive — Form paragraph 7.95 (bona fide, non-responsive amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply filed is not fully responsive to the prior Office action but appears bona fide, applicant is given a TIME PERIOD of ONE (1) MONTH or THIRTY (30) DAYS from the mailing date of the notice, whichever is longer, to supply the omission or correction to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of this time period may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a). This practice does not apply where there has been a deliberate omission of necessary part of a complete reply or where the application is subject to a final Office action—then the examiner has no authority to grant an extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of arguments in response — Form paragraph 7.95.01
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant's reply lacks arguments, applicant should submit an argument under the heading 'Remarks' pointing out disagreements with the examiner’s contentions and must discuss the references applied against the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must explain how the claims avoid or distinguish from the cited references. This paragraph supports treating an otherwise bona fide but argument-deficient reply as nonresponsive and requesting completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims presented with no attempt to point out patentable novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: In amended cases where no attempt is made to point out the patentable novelty, the claims should not be allowed (see 37 CFR 1.111 and MPEP § 714.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment failing to point out the patentable novelty may be held not fully responsive and a time period set to furnish a proper reply; however, if claims as amended are clearly open to rejection on the record, a final rejection should generally be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate inspection checklist for filed amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions by applicant, especially those filed near the end of the reply period, should be inspected immediately to determine whether they are completely responsive and to prevent abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should check: (A) proper signature (MPEP § 714.01(a)); (B) filed within statutory/shortened period (MPEP § 710–§ 710.05); (C) fully responsive and complies with 37 CFR 1.121 (MPEP §§ 714.03–714.04); (D) whether changes warrant transfer (MPEP § 903.08(d)); (E) if application is special (MPEP § 708.01); (F) if interference-suggested claims were copied (MPEP § 2305); (G) traversal of restriction requirement (MPEP § 818.03(a)); (H) use of nonpermanent paper (MPEP § 714.07); (I) applicant-cited references (MPEP § 707.05(b), § 1302.12); (J) terminal disclaimer filed (MPEP §§ 508.01, 804.02, 804.03, 1490); (K) added security related matter (MPEP § 115).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental action when amendment crosses in the mail
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental action is usually necessary when an amendment is filed on or before the mailing date of the regular action but reaches the Technology Center later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental action should be promptly prepared; need not reiterate all applicable portions of the previous action but should specify which portions are to be disregarded and state that the period for reply runs from mailing of the supplemental action. The action should be headed 'Responsive to amendment of (date) and supplemental to the action mailed (date).' See MPEP § 714.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments not in permanent ink (37 CFR 1.52(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.52(a) requires 'permanent dark ink or its equivalent' for papers that become part of the record; documents on 'easily erasable' paper violate the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If noncompliant, applicant is promptly notified that the amendment is not entered and required to file a permanent copy within 1 month or order the PTO to make a copy at applicant's expense. Physical entry of the amendment will be made from the permanent copy. If no response, PTO may make a copy and charge applicant. Good direct/indirect copies (photocopy, facsimile) on satisfactory paper acceptable, but original signatures (if required) must be applied after copy is made. See MPEP § 608.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telegraphic amendments not accepted as replies
rubrics_metrics.description: When a telegraphic amendment (telegram) is received, the telegram is placed in the file but not entered; applicant will be notified that the telegram is not accepted as a reply to the previous Office action and is not entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time period for reply continues to run and is extendable under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims added in excess of filing fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims added in excess of the filing fee may be presented on payment of an additional fee (see MPEP § 607).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excess claims may be presented any time after the application is filed, including before the first action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after final rejection or action (37 CFR 1.116) — permissible content
rubrics_metrics.description: After final rejection or other final action, amendments may be made canceling claims or complying with any requirement of form expressly set forth in a previous Office action; amendments presenting rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal may be admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission or refusal to admit amendments after final does not relieve the application from its status as subject to appeal or save it from abandonment under § 1.135. No amendment as a matter of right in appealed cases; after decision on appeal, amendments only as provided in §§ 1.198 and 1.981 or to carry into effect certain recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of post-final amendments touching merits — good and sufficient reasons required
rubrics_metrics.description: If amendments touching the merits are presented after final rejection (or after appeal has been taken) they may be admitted upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons why they are necessary and were not earlier presented (37 CFR 1.116(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily amendments filed after final are not entered unless approved by the examiner; compliance with the showing under 37 CFR 1.116(c) is expected for such amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on further prosecution after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a final rejection that is not premature has been entered, applicant no longer has a right to unrestricted further prosecution; however, amendments that place the application in condition for allowance or in better form for appeal may be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments complying with objections or requirements as to form are to be permitted after final action in accordance with 37 CFR 1.116(b). Failure to properly reply under 37 CFR 1.113 to a final rejection results in abandonment. A reply under 37 CFR 1.113 is limited to: (A) an amendment complying with 37 CFR 1.116; (B) a Notice of Appeal (and fee); or (C) an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 with a submission that meets 37 CFR 1.111 and fee set in 37 CFR 1.17(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended applicant practices to ease after-final prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are advised to include at filing or no later than the first reply claims varying from the broadest claim to the most detailed claim they are willing to accept to alleviate difficulties encountered after final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily only one personal interview after final should be entertained, with a second permitted only in exceptional circumstances if it would materially assist in placing the application in condition for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory period/advisory action timing and extension-fee computation
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant initially replies within 2 months of a final rejection setting a 3-month shortened statutory period and the Office does not mail an advisory action until after the end of the 3-month period, the period for reply for purposes of calculating any extension fee will be the date the advisory action is mailed, but in no event later than six months from the date of the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required wording must be included in final rejections (form paragraphs 7.39, 7.40, 7.40.01, 7.41, 7.41.03, and 7.42.09). If first reply is not filed within 2 months, any extension fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a) is calculated from the end of the reply period set in the final rejection. Failure to file within the shortened statutory period results in abandonment unless time is extended under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner action when proposed post-final amendment does not place case in better form
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposed amendment does not place the case in better form for appeal or condition for allowance, applicant should be promptly informed, whenever possible, within the statutory period; refusal to enter should not be arbitrary and reasons should be concisely expressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of concise reasons for nonentry: (A) claims would not avoid the rejections set forth in the last Office action and thus would not place the case in condition for allowance or in better condition for appeal; (B) claims would raise new matter; (C) claims present new issues requiring further consideration or search; (D) amendment presents additional claims without canceling any finally rejected claims and so does not improve condition for appeal. Examiner should indicate status of each claim and which proposed claims would be entered on filing of an appeal if filed separately. Applicant should be notified of acceptable portions that would place some claims in better form for appeal or comply with form objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory and allowability notices; examiner response times for post-final amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Action form PTOL-303 should be used to acknowledge receipt of a reply after final rejection that does not place the application in condition for allowance. Notice of Allowability form PTOL-37 should be used when claims are placed in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner is expected to turn in a response to an amendment after final rejection within 10 calendar days from receipt by the examiner and to mail a reply within 30 days of receipt. Prompt notice to applicant may avoid unnecessary appeals and prevent abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of no appeal or no proper amendment after final
rubrics_metrics.description: If no appeal has been filed within the period for reply and no amendment has been submitted to make the application allowable or which can be entered in part, the application stands abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 37 CFR 1.181 petition will not stay the period for reply to an examiner’s action. See MPEP §§ 1207, 706.07(f), 714.13, and related sections for appeal and post-appeal procedures and for after-final affidavit/declaration practice (MPEP §§ 715.09 and 716).
